title: Package checking with rhub::rc_submit() fails due to vignette building
description:
I encountered a problem related to the building of vignettes for my package (`graph4lg`) when checking it on several platforms using `rhub::rc_submit()`.
The checking works locally when running `R CMD check --as-cran graph4lg_2.0.0.tar.gz` and also with `devtools::check_win_release()`

With rhub, I get the following error ([see here](https://github.com/r-hub2/strengthened-confidential-fruitfly-graph4lg/actions/runs/28929623001/job/85825353544)):

```
Warning in file(con, "w") :
  cannot open file 'C:/Users/RUNNER~1/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpotweLo/Rinst23702c8021ac/00LOCK-graph4lg/00new/graph4lg/doc/index.html': No such file or directory
Error: Error in file(con, "w") : cannot open the connection
ERROR: installing vignettes failed
* removing 'C:/Users/RUNNER~1/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpotweLo/Rinst23702c8021ac/graph4lg'
```

Note that I had followed the advice given [here](https://ropensci.org/blog/2019/12/08/precompute-vignettes/) and pre-compiled the vignettes using a vignette.Rmd.orig file to generate a pre-compiled vignette.Rmd file and figures folders. But this did not solve my problem.

I would be very glad if you could indicate me what would be the best way to go forward in checking my package prior to resubmission to CRAN?

title: Quarto installation
description:
When `DESCRIPTION` contains `VignetteBuilder: quarto`, the default `rhub::rhub_setup()` template fails with 

    
    Error: processing vignette 'VIGNETTE_NAME.qmd' failed with diagnostics:
      Quarto binary is required to build Quarto vignettes but is not available.
      ℹ Please make sure it is installed and found by `find_quarto()`.

This may be addressed by adding,  conditional on `VignetteBuilder: quarto`:

```yml 
  linux-containers:
    needs: setup
    if: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.containers != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: ${{ matrix.config.label }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config: ${{ fromJson(needs.setup.outputs.containers) }}
    container:
      image: ${{ matrix.config.container }}

    steps:
      - uses: r-hub/actions/checkout@v1
      - uses: r-hub/actions/platform-info@v1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.RHUB_TOKEN }}
          job-config: ${{ matrix.config.job-config }}
      - uses: r-hub/actions/setup-deps@v1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.RHUB_TOKEN }}
          job-config: ${{ matrix.config.job-config }}

      - uses: dcarbone/install-jq-action@v4.0.1

      - name: Quarto installation - provide dummy 'sudo'
        run: |
          if ! command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo '#!/bin/sh' > /usr/local/bin/sudo
            echo 'exec "$@"' >> /usr/local/bin/sudo
            chmod +x /usr/local/bin/sudo
          fi

      - name: Detect OS distribution
        id: os-check
        run: |
          if [ -f /etc/os-release ]; then
            . /etc/os-release
            case "$ID" in
              fedora|rhel|centos|rocky|almalinux)
                echo "is_fedora=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
                ;;
              *)
                echo "is_fedora=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
                ;;
            esac
          else
            echo "is_fedora=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      # UBUNTU
      - name: Fetch Ubuntu dependencies needed by Quarto dynamic binary
        if: ${{ steps.os-check.outputs.is_fedora != 'true' }}
        run: |
          apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y -qq wget libc6

      - if: ${{ steps.os-check.outputs.is_fedora != 'true' }}
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2

      # FEDORA
      - name: Fetch Fedora dependencies needed by Quarto dynamic binary
        if: ${{ steps.os-check.outputs.is_fedora == 'true' }}
        run: |
          dnf install -y wget glibc glibc-common libstdc++ tar || yum install -y wget glibc libstdc++ tar

      - name: Install Quarto CLI via Tarball (Fedora)
        if: ${{ steps.os-check.outputs.is_fedora == 'true' }}
        run: |
          QUARTO_URL=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/latest | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name | endswith("linux-amd64.tar.gz")) | .browser_download_url')

          if [ -z "$QUARTO_URL" ] || [ "$QUARTO_URL" = "null" ]; then
            QUARTO_URL="https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.5.57/quarto-1.5.57-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
          fi

          mkdir -p /opt/quarto
          curl -sL "$QUARTO_URL" | tar -xz -C /opt/quarto --strip-components=1

          ln -sf /opt/quarto/bin/quarto /usr/local/bin/quarto

      - name: Configure Quarto environment
        run: |
          QUARTO_BIN=$(command -v quarto || echo "/opt/quarto/bin/quarto")
          QUARTO_DIR=$(dirname "$QUARTO_BIN")
          echo "QUARTO_PATH=$QUARTO_BIN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "QUARTO_BIN_PATH=$QUARTO_DIR" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Pre-install package for Quarto vignette subprocess
        run: R CMD INSTALL .
        shell: bash
      - uses: r-hub/actions/run-check@v1
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.RHUB_TOKEN }}
          job-config: ${{ matrix.config.job-config }}

  other-platforms:
    [...]
      - uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
      - name: Pre-install package for Quarto vignette subprocess
        run: R CMD INSTALL .
        shell: bash
      - uses: r-hub/actions/run-check@v1
        with:
          job-config: ${{ matrix.config.job-config }}
          token: ${{ secrets.RHUB_TOKEN }}
```

As this involves a fair bit of complexity, I wonder whether the best approach would be to include a new action that templates this away, that is included in the default template, and that includes a check for VignetteBuilder: quarto as a gate for the installation thereof?

title: Cannot recreate VALGRIND issues that CRAN found
description:
Hi,

I've run VALGRIND checks with rhub, using `rhub::rhub_check("https://github.com/tony-aw/broadcast_testing", "valgrind")`, on my R package.
But it cannot recreate the VALGRIND issues that CRAN found.

- CRAN's VALGRIDM output: https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/memtests/valgrind/broadcast/tests/tinytest.Rout -> see the several "Invalid write of size  " issues it found.

- rhub issues: https://github.com/tony-aw/broadcast_testing/actions/runs/30648539419/job/91215946072 -> `run-check@v1` -> `output` -> `Show output of examples and tests`.

Why the difference? How can I recreate the issues CRAN found?

The only thing worth mentioning is that rhub runs less tests for time constraints, but I made sure it ran all tests where CRAN found issues in, and I added a few tests for extra diagnostics.

Thanks in advance for your response!

Kind regards,

Tony

I know I routinely forget to add it myself anyhow!  Just a thought, thanks for a great package :)

title: rhub_check() fails in processing a vignette.
description:
I need to to build a Windoze binary of a package that I am developing.
I tried to do this using rhub v2.  First,  I created a github repository for the package,
explicitly https://github.com/rolfTurner/kanova.   Then I went to the local (cloned) directory for the package, started R, and executed

library(rhub)
rhub_check(platforms="windows")

After some time, failure was reported.  The problem seems to be with
the vignette.   I pre-compiled the vignette, doing

    pdflatex testStat.ltx

in the vignettes directory.   This creates a file testStat.pdf in that directory.  In "ordinary circumstances" (doing a local build), the build uses this pre-compiled file (i.e. testStat.pdf).

However when I use rhub_check(), the system seems not to use
testStat.pdf, tries to re-compile testStat.ltx and complains that
pdflatex is not available.   See the screenshot:

![Screenshot 2024-08-02 at 11-20-32 incredulous-allosaurus windows · rolfTurner_kanova@1444609](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8ee6abc-5b0b-44a5-9945-e2365091ca1b)

Is there any way to either:

(a) get rhub_check() to use the pre-compiled file testStat.pdf, or
(b) make pdflatex available to rhub_check() ?

Thanks for any ideas.

title: `macos` builder failing: "The macOS-13 based runner images are now retired"
description:
I encountered a failure when attempting to run checks using the `macos` platform. It appears that the underlying GitHub Actions runner image (`macos-13`) has been officially retired as of early December, causing the job to fail immediately during initialization.

The command I used was:
```r
rhub::rhub_check(platforms = "macos")
```

The build logs return the following error:
```
The macOS-13 based runner images are now retired. For more details, see https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13046.
The macOS-13 based runner images are being deprecated, consider switching to macOS-15 (macos-15-intel) or macOS 15 arm64 (macos-latest) instead. For more details see https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/13046
```

Thanks for maintaining rhub!

title: Better motivate the package
description:
Hi, I inherited using `rhub::check_for_cran()` from another maintainer's release process and kept it up from inertia.

As I approach a new release, I'm wondering "do I need this step?" and turned to the package website to try and answer this.

I found the README summary less than compelling:

> R-hub v2 uses GitHub Actions to run R CMD check and similar package checks. The rhub package helps you set up R-hub v2 for your R package, and start running checks.

I don't really see why I would go out of my way to use this. I think it makes sense to try and write down some better / self-contained motivation for the package in the README as a pitch for using the tooling.

title: Error: R CMD check found ERRORs for macos and macOS-arm64 but not linux or windows.
description:

The job and logs are here: 
https://github.com/OpenDendro/dplR/actions/runs/13044039594/job/36391482813

I am aware of the array size warnings (e.g., [line 112](https://github.com/OpenDendro/dplR/actions/runs/13044039594/job/36391482714)) but don't know if that is connected to the error. The linux compiler is not concerned with `-fmax-stack-var-size` nor is the windows compiler.

title: Git not installed on containers (/git submodules)
description:
Git seems to not be installed on at least GCC14 & clang19 containers when the repo gets checked out (step `r-hub/actions/checkout@v1`).

I encountered this originally because I was testing git submodules, and manually added `submodules: true` to that step in the workflow file. This then led the action to fail (`Input 'submodules' not supported when falling back to download using the GitHub REST API. To create a local Git repository instead, add Git 2.18 or higher to the PATH.`). I checked afterwards and even without submodules, checkouts output contains this: `The repository will be downloaded using the GitHub REST API
To create a local Git repository instead, add Git 2.18 or higher to the PATH`.

My first workaround attempt was running `git submodule update --init --recursive` after the checkout, but this then gave the error `/__w/_temp/f02433a2-2220-4eaa-8f18-86cf765ab970.sh: line 1: git: command not found`. After some debugging (`which git`/`git --version`) it seemed git was not installed on the container.

The second attempt was adding git as `SystemRequirements` to the DESCRIPTION file (following #600) and running the submodule update after `r-hub/actions/setup-deps@v1`. This kind of works, the problem here is that the original checkout doesn't create a local git repository (since fallback to REST API) so the submodule update returns: `fatal: not a git repository`.

My solution now is to install git via the package manager in a step before checkout (then `submodules: true` works), but this is of course not great with the different containers (dnf for gcc14, apt-get for clang19, etc.).

When running `rhub_check()` for Fedora platforms, the `setup-deps` step fails for me when trying to locate `pak`:

https://github.com/CHOP-CGTInformatics/REDCapTidieR/actions/runs/8649035798

Rhub v2 is working great for all other platforms. I tested at least one other linux container (clang-asan) so this doesn't appear general to all linux containers vs. other platforms.

I suspect the issue is with `renv` causing `pak` to be installed in a place that `library(pak, lib.loc = Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"))` can't detect.

I'm using `rhub_2.0.0` from CRAN.

title: clang17 checking not covered
description:
Dear Rhub,
I recently updated one of my CRAN packages and received the warning:
```
[...]
The auto-check found additional issues for the *last* version released on CRAN:
  clang17 <https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/clang17/rlibkriging.log>
  clang17 <https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/clang17/rlibkriging.out>
[...]
```
So I tried to reproduce the problem with rhub/debian-clang-devel , but without sucess.
It seems that beyond **clang**, it also misses **flang** to reveal my portability issue.
So I had to slightly modify debian-clang-devel with following conf :

```
# Install llvm17
apt-get update
apt-get install lsb-release wget software-properties-common gnupg
wget https://apt.llvm.org/llvm.sh
chmod +x llvm.sh
./llvm.sh 17
apt-get install flang-17 

# Setup Makevars to match clang CRAN test
mkdir -p ~/.R
touch ~/.R/Makevars
echo "CC=clang-17" >> ~/.R/Makevars
echo "CXX=clang++-17" >> ~/.R/Makevars
echo "FC=flang-new-17" >> ~/.R/Makevars
```

I don't know if the purpose of this image is really to cover the clang17 CRAN checking, but at least this could help people like me to reproduce the check warning.

Regards.

title: R won't build with MKL suggested options using ICX/ICPX
description:
Hi,

Intel One API are moving away from ICC/ICPC towards ICX/ICPX (they mainly have moved away from it already).

When trying to build R today I have been doing the following with the Intel Classic Compiler (ICC):

export CC=icc
export FC=ifort
export F77=ifort
export CXX=icpc
export CXXFLAGS="-std=c++17"
export CFLAGS=-O3

./configure --prefix=/local/software/R/4.3.1/install/ --with-blas=-qmkl=parallel --with-lapack=-qmkl=parallel --enable-R-shlib --with-x=no --with-pcre1 --with-cairo

make -j16
make install

Which works without issues, aside from obvious complaints that I shouldn't be using ICC as it is deprecated.

When I do the same but 

**export CC=icx**
export FC=ifort
export F77=ifort
**export CXX=icpx**
export CXXFLAGS="-std=c++17"
export CFLAGS=-O3

title: I wasn't able to reproduce the CRAN clang asan ubsan warnings and errors using the Fedora rhub docker image
description:
First of all thank you for making this repository publicly available.

I currently have clang asan ubsan issues with a couple of my RcppArmadillo packages (OpenImageR, fastGLCM) and I used one of the rhub docker images (`rhub/fedora-clang-devel-san`) to reproduce and fix these issues. I wasn't sure if I have to open the issue here or in the [rhub-linux-builders](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub-linux-builders) repository

I realized that reproducing the clang-asan-ubsan issues is not feasible because currently the rhub dockerfile uses by default the [fedora:33 docker image](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub-linux-builders/blob/master/fedora/Dockerfile#L3) whereas the latest [Fedora version is 37 ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedora_Linux_release_history). I was able to retrieve this fedora version also from the [Docker API](https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/fedora/tags)

I am aware of the [related rhub issue](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub/issues/464) where the fedora version was set to version 33 in the Dockerfile, because I received initially also the `R_HOME ('/opt/R-devel/lib64/R') not found` error and during my search on the web I stumbled upon the cause which I also describe in the README.md file of the [repository that I created (by including the url's)](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan#fedora_clang_rdsan). This seems to be a 'glibc' issue (as mentioned in the thread). The temporary solution (proposed in the thread) was to include one of the following two commands in the docker run command (runtime):

* `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined`
* `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`

What I did in my repo was to include an [R script](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan/blob/master/fedora_latest_version.R) to retrieve the latest Fedora version (currently 37) using the Docker API and to also slightly modify the 3 related Dockerfiles from the [rhub-linux-builders](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub-linux-builders) repository ([Dockerfile_fedora](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan/blob/master/Dockerfile_fedora), [Dockerfile_fedora_clang](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan/blob/master/Dockerfile_fedora_clang), [Dockerfile_fedora_clang_san](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan/blob/master/Dockerfile_fedora_clang_san)). Thank you for all your work. Then I created a [new Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/mlampros/fedora_clang_san) based on the latest fedora version which by default installs the LLVM-Clang version 14.0.5 which is close to the one used currently [by CRAN (14.0.6) on Fedora 34](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/memtests/README.txt). This docker image is created using a [Github action](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan/blob/master/.github/workflows/gh_action.yml)

Based on [this docker image](https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/mlampros/fedora_clang_san) I was able to reproduce the CRAN Clang asan ubsan issues in both packages (OpenImageR, fastGLCM) [both from the command line and from within an R session](https://github.com/mlampros/fedora_clang_rdsan#how-to-use-the-asan-ubsan-docker-image)

I don't know how rhub works internally but there might be a quick fix using one of the two runtime commands 

* `--cap-add=SYS_PTRACE --security-opt seccomp=unconfined`
* `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined`

I'll ping the ones that might be interested in this issue (based on [issue 464](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub/issues/464) and [issue 462](https://github.com/r-hub/rhub/issues/462))
@gaborcsardi
@maelle

title: Fedora using V8 package
description:
I don't know if this is an r-hub issue or a V8 issue; I'll start here.

I am prepping the vegawidget package for another CRAN release. According to CRAN, there are [no problems on Fedora](https://cran.rstudio.org/web/checks/check_results_vegawidget.html) for vegawidget (0.4.1.) All the checks are passing using GitHub Actions, and on the other `rhub::check_for_cran()` default platforms.

However, using rhub's `"fedora-gcc-devel"`, I get a V8-related problem for both the existing CRAN version of vegawidget (0.4.1), and the dev version (proposed for CRAN):

```
 >   svg <- vw_to_svg(vegawidget(spec_mtcars))
 Error in context_eval(join(src), private$context, serialize, await) : 
   SyntaxError: Use of const in strict mode.
 Calls: vw_to_svg ... <Anonymous> -> evaluate_js -> get_str_output -> context_eval
 Execution halted
```

Links to vegawidget runs on r-hub `"fedora-gcc-devel"`: [CRAN](https://builder.r-hub.io/status/vegawidget_0.4.1.tar.gz-839eeb86f477401f93425b6198be7ea0) and [dev](https://builder.r-hub.io/status/vegawidget_0.4.1.9002.tar.gz-f87a78eee39a46a3ad468da21064e21d).

I understand that curating the versions of `libv8` for all these platforms is an ongoing challenge, so I hope @jeroen won't mind that I cc him, here.

There is no great urgency to this. I'd like to make a CRAN release at some point, but there are no deadlines.

Of course, I remain grateful for all that r-hub does to support development efforts, and all that @jeroen does to keep V8 up and running. Thanks as always!

````

title: Sanitizer image defaults to gnu++98
description:
Hello,
since R 4.3, `C++17` is the default and CMD check raises a note if an older standard (e.g. `C++11`) is specified.
Consequently I removed this from my package, but when submitting via `check_with_sanitizers` I get compiler errors and I see in the logs that g++ receives `-std=gnu++98`.
I am not super familiar with docker but I assume this is because the original r-devel-san image has `CXXSTD=-std=gnu++98` hardcoded?

For now I workaround this by re-adding the `C++11` specification for just the sanitizer image check and removing it again afterwards (I guess you could also just specify `C++17` since that shouldn't raise a note with CMD check).

title: Handle noisy compiler output
description:
One of my packages links to `RcppEigen`, which generates a huge volume ~10,000 lines of noisy but irrelevant warnings (e.g. unknown pragma) by default, as of course required by CRAN. This relates to https://github.com/r-hub/rhub/issues/42 .

With some gymnastics, I can send R CMD INSTALL args via R CMD check args, via `rhub::check`, but these only apply to the tested package itself, not dependencies. There is no way I can find to pass any compiler flags to an rhub docker build. As was suggested in https://github.com/r-hub/rhub/issues/42 , folding sections in the HTML output would be a workaround.

No doubt more complicated would be configurable compiler flags for both package itself and dependencies. Or possibly, optionally passing a custom`~/.R/Makevars` through.

title: Adapt `local_check_linux()` to run with docker alternative like `podman` ?
description:
I tried `podman` which is an alternative for `docker`, and from doc it was supposed to be a 1-1 equivalent mainly , meaning something that run with `docker` runs with `podman`

https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2019/02/21/podman-and-buildah-for-docker-users

I did a quick test: 
* I add this in `rhub-linux.sh` (by modifying my local install of **rhub**)
````sh
docker() {
    /usr/bin/podman "$@"
}
````
* then I ran `rhub::local_check_linux(image = "rhub/debian-gcc-devel")`

Everything worked as expected, (except running manually the image at the end because it seems that `podman` does not use name but only id). 

Anyway, having a way to configure a docker alternative would be great to benefit from this feature of running local checks in container. 

Just throwing the idea for this, either for support or just a switch that could allow advanced _at your own risk_ usage.

title: gsl-config not found on linux/debian?
description:
First off, thank you for all you do to provide and maintain the r-hub/rhub service!  I do appreciate it.  I have tinkered, researched, and submitted several times to try and answer my own question, and I'm hoping it is a quick answer so as to not take up too much of your time.  If it does look like it will take up too much -- feel free to just point in another direction to try on my own.

I have an R-package right now that is being developed privately, otherwise, I'd include some reproducible examples.  Here goes --

When I run `rhub::check_on_windows()`, the entire check is successful.  My `Makevars.win` looks like

````
GSL_CFLAGS = -I$(LIB_GSL)/include

ifeq "$(WIN)" "64"
GSL_LIBS = -L$(LIB_GSL)/lib/x64 -lgsl -lgslcblas
else
GSL_LIBS = -L$(LIB_GSL)/lib/i386 -lgsl -lgslcblas
endif

# combine with standard arguments for R
PKG_CPPFLAGS = $(GSL_CFLAGS)
PKG_LIBS = $(GSL_LIBS)
````

With windows successful, I'll set it aside.  Let's move onto Solaris.  When I run `rhub::check_on_solaris()`, I get a successful check as well with this `Makevars` (let's call it for the sake of this trouble shooting "Makevars-form-1"):

  * Makevars-form-1

````
PKG_CPPFLAGS=-I$(LIB_GSL)/include
PKG_LIBS=-L$(LIB_GSL)/lib -lgsl -lgslcblas
````

I also have a successful check with `rhub::check_on_solaris()` using the trick from [Section 1.6 of R-exts](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-exts.html#Writing-portable-packages) that talks about backticks and `gsl-configure` -- the `Makevars` looks like this (we'll labels it Makevars-form-2):

  * Makevars-form-2

````
PKG_CPPFLAGS=`gsl-config --cflags`
PKG_LIBS=`gsl-config --libs`
````

I have yet a third (!) style which uses a configure file that looks for `gsl-config` and then if found gets the information from its output.  Let's call this Makevars-form-3:

* Makevars-form-3

````
GSL_CFLAGS = @GSL_CFLAGS@
GSL_LIBS = @GSL_LIBS@
PKG_LIBS=$(GSL_LIBS)
PKG_CFLAGS=$(GSL_CFLAGS)
````

with the `configure.ac` made into `configure` with a run of `autoconf` in Terminal that uses the pattern popularized by the [RcppGSLExample](https://github.com/eddelbuettel/rcppgsl/tree/master/inst/examples/RcppGSLExample) approach.  I put an echo statement to print out the values and this is the output:

````
#> --------------------------------------------------

 120#> GSL_CFLAGS: -I/opt/csw/include

 121#> GSL_LIBS: -L/opt/csw/lib -lgsl -lgslcblas -lm

#> --------------------------------------------------
````

Okay.  So at this point I have 3 different forms for identifying the location of GSL which lead to successful checks on solaris.  Moreover, as a bonus, all 3 forms of Makevar lead to successful checks with `rhub::check(platform="macos-highsierra-release-cran")`, and I include the echo statement for Makevar-form-3:

````

title: Windows machines should define CXX14 and CXX14STD
description:
R packages requiring C++14 currently do not pass on rhub, but do pass on win-builder. Even though both use RTools34, on win-builder `CXX14` and `CXX14STD` are defined. That prevents you from getting this error, which you do get on rhub:

```
C++14 standard requested but CXX14 is not defined
```

The suggestions from Jeroen is to set the following in `~/.R/Makevars.win` (or is it just `~/.R/Makevars`? I'm not sure):

- `CXX14 = g++`
- `CXX14STD = -std=gnu++1y`
- We are not sure about `gnu++1y`, which win-builder might be setting to `gnu++14` instead, but I think either will work.

See this issue for a little bit more information:
https://github.com/r-windows/r-testing/issues/1#issue-379473228

title: Solaris doesn't support --donttest
description:
When preparing for CRAN release I often use `check_args = "--as-cran --run-donttest"`. Checking on solaris I got the error `./rhub-env.sh: line 1: --run-donttest: command not found` right at the start (L18). This doesn't occur if I test on windows platforms

Alternatively, if I test on solaris with `check_args = "--as-cran"` it starts the test as expected.

To summarize:

**Tests start as expected**
```
rhub::check_for_cran(path = "../weathercan_0.3.2.tar.gz",
                     check_args = "--as-cran",
                     platforms = "solaris-x86-patched",
                     show_status = FALSE)

rhub::check_for_cran(path = "../weathercan_0.3.2.tar.gz",
                     check_args = "--as-cran --run-donttest",
                     platforms = c("windows-x86_64-oldrel",
                                   "windows-x86_64-devel",
                                   "windows-x86_64-release"),
                     show_status = FALSE)
```

**Tests result in early errors**

```
rhub::check_for_cran(path = "../weathercan_0.3.2.tar.gz",
                     check_args = "--as-cran --run-donttest",
                     platforms = "solaris-x86-patched",
                     show_status = FALSE)
```

title: Difference between check_with_sanitizers() and CRAN checks with sanitizers
description:
Thanks so much for this wonderful service!

After submitting a package I have been checking with `check_with_sanitizers()` to CRAN, I received notification that it failed the tests with their build machines with sanitizers. After some exploration today, I discovered that the difference is that there is no detection of `alloc-dealloc-mismatch` on rhub.

I made a [minimal package](http://github.com/gergness/rookie) to demonstrate this - when run on rhub, there is no error, but on CRAN there would be an error like: 
```
  Running ‘testthat.R’
 ERROR
Running the tests in ‘tests/testthat.R’ failed.
Last 13 lines of output:

title: Expose check results in a more machine-readable format
description:
**Current behavior**
Currently publicly exposed methods for investigating `rhub_check` objects seem to be mostly  side-effecting (printing) with different levels of detail, which is great for interactive use.

**Desired feature**
When processing `check` results using code (e.g. for CI/CD purposes) it would however be useful if the results were exposed in a more machine-readable format.

**Further context, use case, examples**
For further context, I currently access the private fields to get to the results like so:

* An [R script that runs the checks](https://gitlab.com/jozefhajnala/jhaddins/blob/experimental/inst/rhubcheck.R) via R-hub and evaluates the results

GitLab CI/CD pipeline context:

* The [.gitlab-ci.yml](https://gitlab.com/jozefhajnala/jhaddins/blob/experimental/.gitlab-ci.yml) that governs the CI/CD pipeline
* An example [of a successful run](https://gitlab.com/jozefhajnala/jhaddins/pipelines/57477509) with checks on 3 platforms

title: rhub update from CRAN
description:
Dear Gábor,

The soon-to-be-release R 4.4.0 has a new function pkg2HTML() in package
tools to create single-page HTML reference manuals for R packages, and
CRAN is planning to start using these HTML refmans on the package web
pages instead of the PDF refmans currently used.

This needs being able to build the HTML refmans without having the
package installed, which currently does not work for your package. 

This can easily be changed: can you please submit a new version of your
package with a new version built with R >= 4.3.0? 

(This will provide Rd expansions for the Rd install/render stage \Sexprs
which may not work when the package is not installed.)

Can you please do so as quickly as possible, and ideally before
2024-04-17?

Best
-k

title: SSL certificate problem on MacOS
description:
I see on Twitter that there were some SSL issues on mac that were resolved in October, however I am still having SSL problems. Whenever I try to work with rhub (e.g. either directly using ``rhub::check_for_cran`` via ``devtools::chech_rhub``) I get this error:

```{R}
Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : 
  SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
```

I am also getting the same error with other web-based functions like ``rhub::validate_email``

I have tried reinstalling rhub and its dependancies, but no luck.

macOS version: 10.14.6 (18G103)
R version: 4.1.2
R Studio version: 1.4.1717

title: Missing `httr` and `keyring` when testing package check --as.cran over 'debian-clang-devel'
description:
Hello, thanks so much for this plateform.
I'm trying to use rhub to do specific check for CRAN to implement a change request received by CRAN team (see https://github.com/eblondel/geometa/issues/200 for the issue occuring with **debian-clang-devel**)

I run rhub through R with `rhub::check_for_cran(path = ".", platforms = "debian-clang-devel")`
Result is here: https://builder.r-hub.io/status/geometa_0.7-1.tar.gz-7e7716d429dc48ed82e232b3d92f0fe6

I get a failure due to missing `httr` and `keyring` package installs. I know `keyring` require some specific systems libs (`libsecret-1-dev`), could it be the reason? but then for `httr` i've no idea what's wrong.

Thanks in advance for your help

title: rHub Solaris different from CRAN Solaris?
description:
Ah Solaris, every R package maintainer's favourite vintage OS - especially if you are using lots of C++ and/or Unicode encodings.

I just updated **quanteda** and the checks show v2.1.2 is [breaking on Solaris on the CRAN results](https://www.r-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-patched-solaris-x86/quanteda-00check.html).

On rHub, though, it's clean:

> **quanteda 2.1.2: NOTE**

>

> 
>

Any ideas as to what causes the difference, and how I might get the correct check in advance?

title: Release rhub 1.1.2
description:
Prepare for release:

* [x] `git pull`
* [x] Check [current CRAN check results](https://cran.rstudio.org/web/checks/check_results_rhub.html)

* [x] `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)`
* [x] `devtools::check_win_devel()`
* [x] `rhub::check_for_cran()`
* [x] `revdepcheck::revdep_check(num_workers = 4)`
* [x] ~~Update `cran-comments.md`~~
* [x] `git push`

Submit to CRAN:

* [x] `usethis::use_version('patch')`
* [x] `devtools::submit_cran()`
* [x] Approve email

Wait for CRAN...

* [x] Accepted :tada:
* [x] `git push`
* [x] `usethis::use_github_release()`
* [x] `usethis::use_dev_version()`
* [x] `git push`

title: update pandoc and/or offer multiple versions
description:
This is a request on behalf of people who use the 'rticles' package to generate a package vignette, or otherwise need recent pandoc features. I seem to need pandoc >= 2.2 for one vignette in my package 'icd'. https://pandoc.org/releases.html says they are currently on 2.7.1 and the CRAN and r-hub version is about 18 months old (version 1.19).

I understand the need to mimic CRAN (just for some builds?). Is a choice of pandoc version possible? Or maybe it is reasonable to offer the latest pandoc in non-CRAN builds and a version similar to CRAN for `check_for_cran` builds.

r-hub does complete the check but with a warning on re-building vignette outputs, so it's not the end of the world. Workarounds I have considered include: not building that particular vignette on CRAN/r-hub at all (but this means I miss out on automated testing of my most intricate, although not computationally heavy vignette, a JSS paper); and asking r-hub not to build vignettes using the environment variable.

title: validate_email() documentation mis-specifies config location
description:
The documentation of `validate_email()` in `R/email.R@9,10` contains the text
```R
#' On your current platform the file is at
#' \Sexpr{rhub:::email_file()}`
```

The Sexpr is executed when the package is compiled – so when downloading the binary package from CRAN, it reads
 >   On your current platform the file is at C:\Users\CRAN\AppData\Local/rhub/rhub/validated_emails.csv.

I'm not sure what the most appropriate fix is: perhaps we need a wrapper for `email_file()` that detects that the package is being built on CRAN, and perhaps replaces the string `C:\Users\CRAN\AppData\Local` with `%APPDATA%`?

title: Update GLPK version in windows-x86_64-release
description:
The `windows-x86_64-release` image contains a copy of GLPK 4.47, which is more than 10 years old now. Would it be possible to update it to a more recent version? The new version of `igraph` depends on GLPK 4.57 or later because it uses `glp_at_error()` and this was added in GLPK 4.57 only (which is also more than 6 years old). If GLPK 4.47 is installed in the image because it matches the version used in the CRAN build environment, then are there any plans to update the CRAN build environment to a newer version in the foreseeable future?

Note that other builders seem to use more recent GLPK versions (4.65 or so), and apparently `rtools-packages` [also contains GLPK 4.65](https://github.com/r-windows/rtools-packages/blob/master/mingw-w64-glpk/PKGBUILD). The commit message even mentions that `glpk` was added because of `igraph`, but it seems like this version is not installed in `windows-x86_64-release` by default.

title: {ps} fails to build on Solaris
description:
I attempted to build `{lightgbm}` (https://github.com/microsoft/LightGBM) on `solaris-x86-patched-ods` tonight, using the following code.

```r
rhub::check(
    path = "lightgbm_3.3.2.99.tar.gz"
    , email = Sys.getenv("EMAIL_FOR_RHUB")
    , check_args = "--as-cran"
    , platform = "solaris-x86-patched-ods"
    , env_vars = c(
        "R_COMPILE_AND_INSTALL_PACKAGES" = "always"
         , "_R_CHECK_SYSTEM_CLOCK_" = 0L
         , "_R_CHECK_CRAN_INCOMING_REMOTE_" = 0L
         , "_R_CHECK_PKG_SIZES_THRESHOLD_" = 60L
         , "_R_CHECK_TOPLEVEL_FILES_" = 0L
    )
    , show_status = TRUE
)
```

That build failed when building `{lightgbm}`'s dependencies. ([build link](https://builder.r-hub.io/status/lightgbm_3.3.2.99.tar.gz-e003453fa4744e8b8d9ac584dfa4cdb7))

`{ps}` fails to build, with the following error:

```text
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘ps’ in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...):
unable to load shared object '/export/home/XeR9Yyk/R/00LOCK-ps/00new/ps/libs/ps.so':
ld.so.1: R: fatal: relocation error: file /export/home/XeR9Yyk/R/00LOCK-ps/00new/ps/libs/ps.so: symbol psll_memory_uss: referenced symbol not found
Error: loading failed
Execution halted
ERROR: loading failed
* removing ‘/export/home/XeR9Yyk/R/ps’
```

Can you help me understand which of these outcomes this failure indicates?

1. The R Hub Solaris environments are no longer supported, and should be considered deprecated.
2. CRAN no longer requires Solaris builds, so releases of packages which don't work on Solaris can make it onto CRAN.
3. There's a mistake in the way I used `rhub::check()`
4. This is a bug in `{ps}`, and should be reported in https://github.com/r-lib/ps instead of here.
5. Something else

Thank you so much for your time, and for maintaining R Hub!

### Debugging Information

From logs like this:

```text
ERROR: dependencies ‘callr’, ‘processx’, ‘ps’ are not available for package ‘testthat’
```

I can see that `{ps}` is required through a chain that starts with `{testthat}`

```text
lightgbm
|_testthat
   |_callr
     |_processx
       |_ps
```

So I suspect that any builds on this environment for packages which use `{testthat}` might be affected.

I can see at https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ps/index.html that there was a new CRAN release of `{ps}` about 3 weeks ago (April 23, 2022), and at https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_ps.html that CRAN did not check that package on Solaris.

I also do not see the Solaris checks listed at https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_summary.html or https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_flavors.html.

So maybe CRAN is no longer requiring Solaris checks, and therefore a `{ps}` release that isn't compatible with Solaris made it to CRAN? If you believe that's the case, then I apologize for taking up your time and attention will consider raising a separate issue with the `{ps}` maintainers.

### References

Build link: https://builder.r-hub.io/status/lightgbm_3.3.2.99.tar.gz-e003453fa4744e8b8d9ac584dfa4cdb7

title: Sorting data
description:
I have some data from robinhood and yahoo finance that i would like to sort. I would like to add the endofday column to my yahoo data. Any tips on how to do this?. Here is my code so far.


library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyquant)

# Vector with names of all unpacked files
# Set an address of a directory with unpacked csv files (1st parameter)
lof <- list.files("robintrack-popularity-history/tmp/popularity_export", full.names = TRUE)

# This function reads and transforms one file
read_data <- function(file){
  
  # get stock name from the name of the file
  stock <- file %>% 
    str_split("/") %>% 
    unlist() %>% 
    last() %>% 
    str_remove(".csv")
  
  read_csv(file,
           col_types = "Td"
           ) %>% 
    mutate(
      date = date(timestamp)
    ) %>% 
    arrange(timestamp) %>% 
    group_by(date) %>% 
    drop_na() %>% 
    summarise(
      endofday = last(users_holding),
      meanday = mean(users_holding)
    ) %>% 
    mutate(
      stock = stock
    )
}

robinhood <- lof %>% 
  map_dfr(read_data)

# Explicit NAs
robinhood <- robinhood %>% 
  complete(date,stock) %>% 
  arrange(stock,date)

save(robinhood, file = "robinhood.RData")

#####################################
# Add data from Yahoo

library(tidyquant)

date_range <- robinhood$date %>% 
  range()

get_yahoo <- function(ss, dr = date_range){
  q <- getSymbols(ss, 
                  from = as.character(dr[1]),
                  to = as.character(dr[2]),
                  warnings = FALSE,
                  auto.assign = FALSE,
                  return.class = "xts")
  
  time_q <- time(q)
  
  q <- q %>% as_tibble()
  
  names(q) <- names(q) %>% 
    str_split("\\.") %>% 
    map_chr(function(x) x[2])
  
  q %>% 
    mutate(
      stock = ss,
      date = time_q
    )
}

get_yahoo_safely <- safely(get_yahoo)

yahoo <- robinhood %>% 
  distinct(stock) %>% 
  pull(stock) %>%
  map(get_yahoo_safely) %>% 
  map_dfr(function(x) x$result)

data_ry <- robinhood %>% 
  left_join(.,yahoo)

save(data_ry, file = "data_ry.RData")

As opposed to checking results only on Windows (`Appveyor`) or on MacOS/linux (`Travis`) machines, `r-hub` provides probably the most comprehensive list of platform checks for continuous integration. 

I was wondering if it would be possible for `r-hub` to create a badge or a table that can be embedded in a `README` file (à la `Appveyor`/`Travis`) or even create a separate vignette just with checks (à la `covrpage`: https://github.com/yonicd/covrpage). This will give a comprehensive summary for all tested platforms, akin to what `CRAN` does (https://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_dplyr.html), but **after every commit**.

Ignore this request if you feel this will be too time consuming or if the returns are marginal over what is already offered by other CI platforms.

title: Non Portable Flags in Solaris Build
description:
Hello,

When checking a build of the R package redist (with sf and spdep dependencies removed), we are coming across the following NOTE: 
```
> checking compilation flags used ... NOTE
  Compilation used the following non-portable flag(s):
    ‘-march=pentiumpro’
```

However, when looking in the contents of the Makevars.in file, we have a pretty standard set up for a package that relies on Rcpp and Rmpi. [Additionally, this links to the file directly](https://github.com/kosukeimai/redist/blob/no-geo-solaris/src/Makevars)
```
PKG_CXXFLAGS = $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS)
PKG_LIBS = $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS) $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS)
```

To my knowledge, this shouldn't be creating the march flag above. Is it possible that this compiler flag is being created by the Solaris machine's options?

[The link to the full check is here.](https://builder.r-hub.io/status/redist_2.0.2.tar.gz-c0e874f6da334100a2a87ad09bb8662e)

Any confirmation that this is (or is not) related to the Rhub machine itself would be very appreciated.

Thanks,
Chris

title: Difference between macos-highsierra-release and idem-cran
description:
Hi,
_I’ve posted this problem on the r-package-devel mailing list at the start of the week (macOS flat namespace)._

I submitted a package to CRAN that I developed in Debian 10, GCC 8, R 3.5. The package needs compilation and links to gdal and proj. It was accepted, and passed all CRAN checks but not those for macOS and OS X flavours ([package](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=uFTIR); [check results](https://cran.r-project.org/web//checks/check_results_uFTIR.html)).

The problem for the r-release-osx-x86_64 platform (macOS 10.13.6, Apple LLVM version 10.0.0 (clang-1000.10.44.4); GNU Fortran (GCC) 8.2.0) looks like:

    ** testing if installed package can be loaded from temporary location
    Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘uFTIR’ in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...):
     unable to load shared object '.../libs/uFTIR.so':
     dlopen(.../libs/uFTIR.so, 6): Symbol not found: _jpeg_resync_to_restart
     Referenced from: .../libs/uFTIR.so
     Expected in: flat namespace
     in .../libs/uFTIR.so
    Error: loading failed

CRAN checks have similar results for the r-oldrel-osx-x86_64 platform (Xcode 8.2.1, clang 4.0.0, GNU Fortran 6.1). However, the not-found symbol is _H5P_CLS_DATASET_CREATE_ID_g

I don’t use any of the objects directly (one comes from libjpeg and the other from HDF5) but they are related with gdal.

I used rhub to reproduce the problem and I got the same output (symbol not found: _jpeg_resync_to_restart) when I send the package to the macos-highsierra-release-cran platform. However, the problem vanishes when I use the macos-highsierra-release (brew) platform. I think that it is a problem with the linked libraries, and I will probably need to adjust the Makevars file(?). However, I’m not quite sure whether this is the problem or not and if it is how to solve it. I couldn't find the difference between the two rhub platforms, thus I though that you could give me an idea… 

The Makevars that works for homebrew but not for the CRAN settings is:

    CXX_STD = CXX11
    PKG_CXXFLAGS = $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS) `pkg-config --cflags gdal`
    PKG_LIBS = $(SHLIB_OPENMP_CXXFLAGS) $(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS) `pkg-config --libs gdal`

I will appreciate your help.

F.

This is with the [checkpoint](https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/checkpoint) package which I've just taken over, whee.

When I run `rhub::check_for_cran()`, the Ubuntu and Fedora tests run OK, but Windows reports a warning when building a vignette:

Error(s) in re-building vignettes:

--- failed re-building 'checkpoint.Rmd'

However, when I run `devtools::install(build_vignettes=TRUE)`, it installs without a problem. This is on a Windows 10 machine.

Looking at the `checkpoint.Rmd` vignette, lines 158-168 are

 ```{r checkpoint, warning=FALSE}
## Create a folder to contain the checkpoint

           checkpointLocation = tempdir())

As far as I can tell, there shouldn't be a problem with this code. Is there something odd about the tempdir location on the Rhub Windows machine?

title: check list improvements
description:
It is not really convenient that this is an R6 object, ideally it should just be a tibble. But there are good reasons for being the data frame, in particular that while the check is running, the status is not known and an R6 object can auto-update itself.

Maybe we want:
- [ ] an `as_tibble()` method
- [ ] custom printing of some columns of that tibble
- [ ] more intuitive way to inspect a single check
- [ ] more intuitive way to inspect a check group

title: A few suggestions & ideas
description:
Hi,

I just started checking `rhub` and it looks very cool! I just have a few comments.

I find https://builder.r-hub.io/ a bit unintuitive. You have to upload a tar ball created by `R CMD build`, right? That might not be so obvious to a new developer.

Second, the man pages of `check()` and similar functions say that `path` can be the tarball built with `R CMD check`. Isn't that `R CMD build`? I see that `rhub:::build_package()` runs `build`.

Third, lets say I'm interested in running checks on a bunch of OS. With any of the `check*` functions used on a directory containing an R package, you end up running `rhub:::build_package()`. It might be nice to export this function or make it more evident that you can run:

```R
library('rhub')
pkgtar <- build_package('my_pkg_dir')
check_on_linux(pkgtar)
check_on_windows(pkgtar)
## Or any other checks
```

Finally, I'm wondering if `rhub` can be tied into Travis in the following way. With Travis you can set up matrix environments, so you can imagine setting a 'platform' environment for several platforms you are interested in checking. Then you configure Travis to install `rhub` and run:

```R
library('rhub')
check('.', platform = Sys.getenv('platform'))
```

That way you use Travis to run `R CMD build` but then use `rhub` for testing on environments beyond linux. To save time, the user would have to setup Travis in such a way that `R CMD check` is disabled.

Best,
Leo

title: Email validation: check() looks in DESCRIPTION and validate_email() in git config
description:
First, I got:

``` r
> validate_email()
Please check your emails for the R-hub access token
token: *********
Token added for ‘hb@aroma-project.org’
```

and then immediately after I got:

``` r
> check()
‘henrikb@braju.com’ is not validated, validating now.
Please check your emails for the R-hub access token
token: 
```

I see that `validate_email()` defaults to Git for my email address, whereas, I assume, `check()` looks at the email address in the `DESCRIPTION` file.

Also, the validation for ‘henrikb@braju.com’ never reaches me. I never have issues with this address. Prior to trying the rhub package, I tried to the online submission and I did recieved a short validation code that worked there.  So, not sure what's going on - could the fact that I did that online validation somehow block the authentication here?

The workaround is to override the DESCRIPTION email as:

``` r
> check(email="hb@aroma-project.org")
[...]
```

which works.

PS. This is all looks neat :)
